pr_title: Fix double template error for service data
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

**Issue #109668 Summary:** Services that define `data` or `data_template` will attempt to render a template twice if the service also defines a `Schema` for the attribute with a template, i.e. `cv.template`. This works fine if a script/automation defines a template for which `is_static` is true, for instance, but results in an incorrect value when the template returns something that has templating characters in it (raising an error for an invalid template or just getting an incorrect value when the template is valid). See below for an example.

This change makes it so the value that's returned when a `Template` is rendered can be type-checked during [schema evaluation in the service call](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/core.py#L2728). The validation can then mark the template that it creates as static so it won't be re-rendered.

This fixes https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/109668.

#### Example

I discovered this when trying to use the notify service to send information about errors appearing in the main log file. Some messages I'm trying to send include errors about failures in templates, and could be truncated. So, for example:

```yaml
service: notify.mobile_app_my_phone
data:
  title: Error in system log
  message: "The following error just occurred: {{ error }}"
```

When `error` is, for example, `Template variable warning: 'name' is undefined when rendering '{% set device_id =...`, message should result in:

```
The following error just occurred: Template variable warning: 'name' is undefined when rendering '{% set device_id =...
```

But the result is that a template error is generated since `message` is re-templated a second time (with the above, which isn't a valid template itself).

I'm not sure about the scope of this issue but the mentioned example in the notify integration has, as far as I know, been deprecated for a long time and we should just replace `cv.template` with `cv.string` in that service schema.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/59637d23913b85ed005befcc15204c0bec202323/homeassistant/components/notify/legacy.py#L159-L168

@MartinHjelmare that sounds reasonable. There are a lot of other services that have `cv.template` in their scheme definition, though. A quick search shows the following components contain the string `cv.template`: `alert`, `alexa`, `arest`, `bayesian`, `camera`, `command_line`, `doods`, `dweet`, `emoncms`, `emulated_kasa`, `generic`, `history_stats`, `homeassistant`, `hp_ilo`, `influxdb`, `intent_script`, `knx`, `logbook`, `logi_circle`, `manual`, `manual_mqtt`, `minio`, `mobile_app`, `mqtt`, `notify`, `rest`, `rest_command`, `rss_feed_template`, `scrape`, `serial`, `slack`, `snmp`, `sql`, `tcp`, `telegram_bot`, `telnet`, `template`, `tensorflow`, `universal`, `velbus`, `xiaomi`.

Also, from what I can tell, the schema is used to validate the script/automation. I'm guessing this is both when saved and when it's run. So I'm not sure if that just creates a giant mess of things based on how the code is currently structured.

Each integration that uses `cv.template` in a service schema, will need to create a repair issue about the deprecation and then eventually replace the use of `cv.template` after the deprecation period is over.

If there are problems with template validation after that, that should be solved centrally by the automation code.

@MartinHjelmare but wouldn't changing them to be strings mean that scripts/automations wouldn't validate the values properly when a user saves changes?

Right now, you get an error saving for malformed templates. How would that get handled if they were changed to `cv.string`?

Automation/script validation is handled by the automation integration and script helper. It's at this stage that the template is handled. When the config reaches the service call and the service schema validation the template has already been rendered to a string.
@MartinHjelmare want to take a look at #122820 as an alternative starting point to resolving the double templating issue?
Closed in favor of #122820 which was just merged into dev.

issue_context.title: Template error with partial template in variable
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The following script generates an error instead of properly escaping the message:

```yaml
alias: Template Error in Variables
sequence:
  - variables:
      partial_template: "{{ '{%' ~ ' set value = ' }}"
  - service: notify.system_error_devices
    data:
      title: Template error example
      message: "{{ partial_template }}"
mode: single
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

_No response_

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
alias: Template Error in Variables
sequence:
  - variables:
      partial_template: "{{ '{%' ~ ' set value = ' }}"
  - service: notify.system_error_devices
    data:
      title: Template error example
      message: "{{ partial_template }}"
mode: single
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Stopped because an error was encountered at February 4, 2024 at 4:00:21 PM (runtime: 0.02 seconds)

invalid template (TemplateSyntaxError: unexpected 'end of template') for dictionary value @ data['message']
```
```

This is still an issue in the latest version. I tested today with:

```
Core 2024.5.2
Supervisor 2024.05.1
Operating System 12.3
Frontend 20240501.1
```

For the case above using the `notify` service:

1. The `data` is rendred [while preparing the service in `async_prepare_call_from_config`][service_prep_render].
1. It is converted back into a `Template` object when the [notify schema][notify_schema] which defines `title` and `message` as `cv.template` [is validated during the service call][service_call_schema_validation].
1. The [`title`][title_render] and [`message`][message_render] renders then happen a second time in [`_async_notify_message_service`][async_notify_message_service].

So this also applies to any service that defines a schema with a `cv.template`. For instance, `logbook.log` is affected as well:

```yaml
- variables:
    partial_template: "{{ '{{ \\'template should not eval\\' }}' }}"
- service: logbook.log
  data:
    name: Example of Double Evaluated Template
    message: "{{ partial_template }}"
```

And also still affected if rendering the data as an object:

```yaml
- service: logbook.log
  data: >
    {{
      {
        'name': 'Test',
        'message': partial_template,
      }
    }}
```

It therefore seems like a solution would be to somehow change the [code that does validation during the service call][service_call_schema_validation] to not re-warp these objects as templates (perhaps only if they've already been rendered?).

Is anyone who is more familiar with the code base able to weigh in?

[notify_schema]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/components/notify/const.py#L33
[service_prep_render]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/helpers/service.py#L417
[service_call_schema_validation]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/core.py#L2728
[title_render]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/components/notify/legacy.py#L263
[message_render]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/components/notify/legacy.py#L272
[async_notify_message_service]: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e1e64be3c9a2597ca17f77ba1ae6c8dbb063eef3/homeassistant/components/notify/legacy.py#L255

As noted above, this appears to only be an issue for services that define a schema. I've used the `demo` component to write a test, but since the test uses the newer `Entity` style notifier, I put all the setup needed to create a service into the test. Basically, the test doesn't live where it should, but does prove the point that the template is evaluated twice.

The branch is at [wbyoung/home-assistant-core@fix-double-template-error](https://github.com/wbyoung/home-assistant-core/tree/fix-double-template-error) and the [test generating the error is here](https://github.com/wbyoung/home-assistant-core/commit/8b304bc1fe1b0f43a03fe48280e185d1d4d85c28#diff-969a2eda5d905ec3929bf17de3b6b7ea9f4399104ce6f6d0a4016c99b31044caR91).

Ok, I added [another test](https://github.com/wbyoung/home-assistant-core/commit/f8a40f2f7b5e3c91af009a12e55d4a4ba27cacf3#diff-69c58b8e869be104a5feafb4843f67bb60009d28f4cc71c82c5ac678c1749ec9R174), wbyoung/home-assistant-core@f8a40f2f7b5e3c91af009a12e55d4a4ba27cacf3, to the `logbook` which seems like a little better of a place to put this that shows that items are being templated twice.

review_comments: Creating a subclass of `str` to allow the type-checking allows the existing code base to gracefully handle the change of return type (unless there are explicit equality checks of `kls == str` anywhere in the codebase instead of using `isinstance`).

Simply flagging the `Template`s generated by `config_validation` functions with `is_static=True` avoids having to change any type expectations by consumers of data processed through the `Schema` validation.
